mechanism: Delegation is a {{work}}-distribution protocol over an existing {{task}}. The delegator sends DELEGATE with the task and its scope; the delegatee replies ACCEPT or REFUSE. Until ACCEPT, the delegator retains ownership. On REFUSE, the delegator reassigns or escalates. On ACCEPT, ownership transfers to the delegatee, which reports PROGRESS via {{heartbeat}}. Completion returns a result. Failure invokes {{break}}; ownership returns to the delegator before retry, reassignment, or escalation.
gloss: Work handoff: delegate → accept/refuse → heartbeat → result-or-failure
failure_modes: No response: The candidate never replies; the delegator retains the task, but work stalls until an external timeout or reassignment policy acts.
Capability mismatch (assigned to incapable agent—fails late).
Circular delegation: A task returns to an earlier owner in its delegation chain.
Overload (one agent accepts everything—need load awareness).
Progress lies (reports complete when not—need verification).
invariants: Delegation is a request, not a command: it is accepted or refused.
Ownership remains with the delegator until ACCEPT; REFUSE transfers nothing and triggers reassignment or escalation.
The delegatee reports progress; silence is not progress.
A failed accepted {{task}} invokes {{break}} and returns ownership to the delegator before the next disposition.
preconditions: Delegator owns the {{task}} and has authority to delegate it.
postconditions: On ACCEPT, ownership transfers to exactly one delegatee; completion returns a result, while failure invokes {{break}} and returns ownership to the delegator.
On REFUSE, the delegator retains ownership and reassigns or escalates the {{task}}.
